claims.statement: 9% of overnight allocations on east-node lanes have been held in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' for more than 90 minutes since 06:00; all other nodes are normal.
claims.corroboration: Single tier-1 verified source from observability owner; sufficient alone per established rule.
claims.limitation: Alert cannot attribute cause; does not show relation to carrier-side confirmation.

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 last night, changing multi-node orders to reserve stock from the east node first; change review passed and regression suite was green.
claims.corroboration: Single tier-1 verified source, owner Inventory Control.
claims.limitation: Passing review/regression does not rule out an unanticipated interaction with carrier pickup handoff.

claims.statement: Held orders were routed to the east node and flagged by the overnight allocator as a split-reservation exception; reports began about 06:00 and continue.
claims.corroboration: Single tier-2 non-authoritative source (customer_support); not corroborated by an authoritative allocation-system record yet.
claims.limitation: Cannot be upgraded to established without a tier-1 source or a second distinct-owner tier<=2 source; conflicts with Inventory Control's informal reconciliation claim in m8_e01.

claims.statement: The v18 east-node-first reservation change is a plausible cause of the stuck east-node orders via split-reservation exceptions blocking release to carrier pickup.
claims.corroboration: Time correlation (v18 live 22:00, issue from 06:00) and lane-scope correlation (east-node only) plus an unverified support report of matching exceptions.
claims.limitation: Correlation only; no discriminating evidence yet. Competing hypotheses (carrier_feed_lag, dock_capacity) not ruled out. Inventory Control's own reconciliation check (m8_e01) reported nothing wrong, which is in tension with C3.

claims.statement: A carrier-side pickup/dock issue (feed lag or capacity) on east-node lanes has not been ruled out; carrier ops on-call found nothing obvious on an initial look at the dock schedule.
claims.corroboration: Incident chat (non-authoritative, informal look) plus a known observability gap: dashboards cannot relate booked pickup state to carrier-side confirmation.
claims.limitation: Very weak; single informal source, no diagnostic run yet. Kept open as an alternative to C4 pending discriminating evidence.

contradictions.claim_a: m8_e01 (Inventory Control: allocation totals reconcile, nothing looks wrong)
contradictions.claim_b: C3 / m8_e10 (support report: held orders flagged as split-reservation exceptions)
contradictions.description: Inventory Control's informal reconciliation check found nothing wrong, but customer support reports every held order was flagged with a split-reservation exception by the overnight allocator. These cannot both be fully accurate as stated.
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: An authoritative, queryable record of allocation exceptions for the held order cohort (not a channel message or a support summary).

next_action.rationale: Directly tests the specific, falsifiable claim in C3/C4 (held orders carry a split-reservation exception from the overnight allocator) against an authoritative system record rather than a support summary or chat. This will either promote C3/C4 toward established/root_cause with discriminating evidence, or refute it and redirect toward the carrier-side hypothesis (C5), and it resolves contradiction X1.
next_action.expected_information_gain: High: distinguishes allocation_rule_defect from carrier-side mechanisms and upgrades or disproves the only concrete mechanism claim currently on the table.
